name: Bicalutamide
mechanism: Non-steroidal anti-androgen - competitive inhibitor of androgen receptors, blocks testosterone and DHT action
dosing: 50mg OD (with LHRH analogue or surgical castration). Locally advanced prostate cancer: 150mg OD as monotherapy
contraindications: Women, children, severe hepatic impairment. Caution in moderate hepatic impairment
interactions: Warfarin (↑ anticoagulant effect - monitor INR closely), midazolam, ciclosporin (affects CYP3A4)
monitoring: LFTs at baseline, monthly for 6 months then periodically. PSA levels. Monitor for gynaecomastia, hepatotoxicity
sideEffects: Hot flushes, gynaecomastia, breast tenderness, decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, hepatotoxicity (rare), fatigue, constipation
pharmacokinetics: Well absorbed orally, long half-life (5-7 days in standard dose, 7-10 days in 150mg), hepatic metabolism, slow elimination
clinicalPearls: Usually given with LHRH agonist (e.g. goserelin) for metastatic prostate cancer. Start 3 days before LHRH agonist to prevent tumour flare. Monitor LFTs closely in first 6 months
indication: Advanced prostate cancer (with LHRH analogue or after surgical castration), locally advanced prostate cancer at high risk of progression
